case.case_title: Palitha v. O.I.C., Police Station, Polonnaruwa and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 880/92, decided on 4 May 1993

clause.text: Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court and detention before trial is not punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s detention constituted unlawful punishment in violation of Article 13(4).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his detention was unlawful and amounted to punishment without trial, infringing Article 13(4).
case_context.respondent_argument: Respondents did not file any objection and did not contest the claim regarding the nature of detention.
key_facts: Petitioner was released on 30.04.1993 after prolonged detention.
No evidence of lawful punishment imposed by a competent court.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that detention before trial is not punishment but must be lawful and not arbitrary; any punishment must be imposed by a competent court.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner was detained without lawful order and not sent for rehabilitation, the detention was found to infringe Article 13(4) protections.
principles_established: Detention before trial is not punishment but must be lawful.
Punishment can only be imposed by a competent court.

outcome.holding: The Court declared that the petitioner’s rights under Article 13(4) were infringed and awarded compensation.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of infringement and Rs. 17,500 compensation.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(4) was materially engaged because the petitioner’s prolonged detention without lawful punishment by a competent court violated the constitutional protections.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The Court granted relief on the basis that detention without lawful order and rehabilitation violated Article 13(4), which limits punishment to competent courts.
